clue.text: Stay in South American boarding house

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south
US is short for the United States, so American
a pension is a continental boarding house

explanation.surface: A traveller lodges for a while in a guest house somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a stay in South America, but South and American are separate abbreviations placed ahead of the boarding house.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution or proceedings is a suspension, a temporary halt.

clue.text: Suspect punched by amateur detective

indicators.note: a punch makes a hole that something is driven into, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: sus is slang for suspect
a ham is an amateur, as in a ham actor or radio ham

explanation.surface: A suspect gets thumped by a private eye who is no professional.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'amateur detective' one phrase; the definition is detective alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamus is American slang for a private investigator or police officer.

clue.text: Drenched with rum, cake's back in tin

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
in places the preceding pieces inside the following one

blocks.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
the final letter of cake
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A rum-soaked cake sits at the back of a baking tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the drink soaking the cake, but it is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means soaked through, thoroughly wet, the same as drenched.

clue.text: Diver's rip fixed with neoprene gum

indicators.note: fixed can mean rigged or repaired, either way the letters are reworked into new order

blocks.note: taken as fodder
taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A scuba diver's torn wetsuit is patched up with neoprene glue.
explanation.walkthrough: The diver is a bird, not a person in a wetsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor penguin is a large Antarctic bird famous for diving to great depths for food.

clue.text: Mad scientists ultimately hallucinate

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: seething means furious, mad in the angry sense
the final letter of scientists

explanation.surface: Crazed scientists end up seeing visions.
explanation.walkthrough: Mad here means angry, not insane.
explanation.definitionFit: To see things is the idiom for perceiving what is not really there, which is to hallucinate.

clue.text: Valuable ring to be melted

blocks.note: O is ring-shaped
to fuse is to melt, or join by melting

explanation.surface: A precious ring is destined for the smelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Valuable ring as one object; Valuable is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of use is useful, worthwhile, which is what valuable means here.

clue.text: 50% off dishes, one with huge chops

indicators.note: taking 50% off means losing half the length of the word, leaving only its first half

blocks.note: crockery is plates and dishes collectively

explanation.surface: A half-price sale on tableware, with someone carving huge chops of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of the eight-letter word for dishes is kept: CROC, informal for crocodile. 'Chops' looks like cuts of meat but means jaws.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile has enormous jaws, and chops is slang for the jaws or mouth of an animal.

clue.text: Tories developed empty rationales for parties

indicators.note: developed means worked up into something new, so the letters change their order
an empty word has lost all its inside letters, leaving only its two ends

blocks.note: these six letters rearranged
the first and last letters of rationales

explanation.surface: Conservatives come up with hollow excuses for their gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: Parties reads as a plural noun, political parties, but it is the verb: to party.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily and boisterously, so roisters means parties as a verb.

clue.text: Prison house in remote part of Spain

blocks.note: the can is slang for prison
Aries is a house, one of the twelve signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A jail building in some far-flung corner of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: House means a sign of the zodiac, the sense astrologers use.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canary Islands, off north-west Africa, are a Spanish territory far from the mainland.

clue.text: Cramped guests registered concern

blocks.note: limited means restricted, short of room
company means visitors or guests

explanation.surface: Visitors squeezed into tight space are anxious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Concern reads as worry but means a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A limited company is a business registered so its owners' liability is limited; a concern is a firm.

clue.text: Total brought to trial in London, one hears

indicators.note: what one hears is the spoken form, so the London pronunciation is what counts

blocks.note: to be had up is to be brought to court; a Cockney drops the h of had

explanation.surface: Someone's case comes to court in the capital and the sums are tallied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had up' means charged in court; in a London (Cockney) accent the h is dropped, giving 'ad up.
explanation.definitionFit: To add up is to total, to find the sum of a set of figures.

clue.text: Dodgy uni tried pocketing Oscar's scholarship

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so these letters are not to be trusted in their given order
to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: these eight letters rearranged
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A shady university has tried to grab a film star's academic award.
explanation.walkthrough: Scholarship here is learning, not a grant; the surface makes it sound like funding that a university pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning, which is one sense of scholarship.

clue.text: Discover a little chateau near Thiepval

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only a small run of their letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of chateau, all of near and the start of Thiepval

explanation.surface: A digger finds something in a French chateau close to Thiepval, a First World War battlefield site on the Somme.
explanation.walkthrough: Thiepval is a village on the Somme, apt for unearthing wartime relics.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig up or find out, which is to discover.

clue.text: English player that's successful, one getting you out?

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a victor is the winner of a contest

explanation.surface: A winning English sportsman asks whether he is the one who gets you out, like a bowler dismissing a batter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a landlord who evicts a tenant gets them out.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is a person, usually a landlord, who legally removes a tenant from a property.

clue.text: Second in line wanting bananas in crepe or egg?

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the following letters have gone mad and must be reordered

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child second in a queue wants banana in a pancake or an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like a filling for the crepe, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince George, elder son of the Prince of Wales, comes after his father in succession to the British throne.

clue.text: Musical fellow turned to producing pictures

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the letters read from the end

blocks.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
cove is old British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A man in show business turns his hand to making films.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces together are reversed. 'Producing pictures' looks like film-making but means bringing images to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocative means bringing strong images or memories to mind, so it is producing mental pictures.

clue.text: Bill claims communication between banks cut

indicators.note: claiming something is taking hold of it, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: an ad is a bill or poster advertisement
a bridge links the two banks of a river

explanation.surface: A bill demands that messages between financial institutions be reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks are river banks, not financial ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Abridged means shortened, as an abridged book is a cut-down version.

clue.text: Rolling Stones prayed, marked with dots of paint

indicators.note: rolling turns something over, so the letters run from the other end

blocks.note: pits are the stones of fruit
pled is a form of pleaded, and to plead is to pray or beg

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones band offered prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: The rock band's name is split: Rolling is the signal and Stones are fruit stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippled describes a surface painted or drawn with many small dots.

clue.text: Behind queen's bed check for sweets

definitions.note: plural, whereas the answer is a mass noun for the sweets

blocks.note: butt is a slang word for the behind
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, plus the 's
a cot is a small bed
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Behind the queen's back, someone inspects her bed in search of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind looks like a preposition but is the noun for one's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard toffee-like confection made from butter and brown sugar.

clue.text: Someone overblowing his runny nose?

blocks.note: surface reading: a person exaggerating, or blowing too hard on a horn
setter's reading: a male patient who makes too much of a common cold

explanation.walkthrough: Overblowing means exaggerating, and blowing his nose fits the cold; the illness is named after the sufferer's sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase mocks men who supposedly treat an ordinary cold as a serious illness.

clue.text: Goes off in leather seat with the top down

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, and moving it down sends it to the end

blocks.note: a saddle is a leather seat for a rider

explanation.surface: Someone drives away in a convertible with leather seats and the roof down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With the top down' looks like a convertible car, but it moves the first letter to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg that addles goes rotten, so addles means goes off.

clue.text: Politician stops using prepared questions

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked on, so the letters are reworked
to stop something can mean to plug it, sitting inside it like a stopper

blocks.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician gives up relying on scripted questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared questions' reads as a single phrase, but 'questions' is a verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to call into question or challenge the truth of something.

clue.text: Trail run that was a mistake, in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
oops is what you say after a mistake

explanation.surface: A jogger admits, looking back, that the cross-country route was a bad choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That was a mistake' is a whole exclamation standing for one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the track or scent left by an animal, which hunters follow as a trail.

clue.text: Marines collected by sailor with small inflatable

indicators.note: being collected by someone means being taken into their keeping, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: RM is the Royal Marines
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
and means together with

explanation.surface: Royal Marines are picked up by a sailor in a little rubber dinghy.
explanation.walkthrough: The small inflatable is a child's swimming aid worn on the arm, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Armbands are small inflatable rings worn on the upper arms by children learning to swim.

clue.text: I see endless plundering around Turkish warzone

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter
turned around, the whole string is read from the other end

blocks.note: taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look or see
pillage is plundering, as a noun

explanation.surface: An observer notes looting going on without end around a battlefield in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Plundering loses its last letter, and the whole string of I, LO and the shortened word is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli, on the Dardanelles in Turkey, was the site of a major First World War campaign.

clue.text: Beheading sanctioned by legislation is shocking

indicators.note: removing a head means the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: something permitted by law is lawful

explanation.surface: Execution by decapitation being legally permitted is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading reads as part of the surface's grim picture, but it tells you to drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful means very bad or appalling, the sense of shocking.

clue.text: Clothing belonging to Pete's mate?

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for clothes
second meaning: Dud was Dudley Moore, partner of Peter Cook in the comedy duo Pete and Dud

explanation.walkthrough: Pete and Dud were the characters of Peter Cook and Dudley Moore, a British comedy double act of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Duds is informal slang for clothes, and read as a possessive it means something owned by Dud.

clue.text: Good guy deters criminal, one taking too much

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
these nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A decent fellow puts off a crook who is helping himself to too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for the person deterred, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy-guts is a glutton, informally a person who eats or takes more than their share.
